heading: Thursday, February 12, 2026
topLine: Mathematicians split on how much AI's Erdős-problem progress means. Also: 2 model releases: MiniMax-M2.5 and OpenAI GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark.

items.headline: Mathematicians split on how much AI's Erdős-problem progress means
items.summary: Scientific American reported mixed assessments of AI's Erdős-problem results. Andrew Sutherland called LLMs useful research tools. Daniel Litt said they produce "a huge amount of garbage" and that individual results have been overhyped online, and Lauren Williams flagged verification as a major problem.

items.headline: MiniMax releases MiniMax-M2.5
items.summary: MiniMax-M2.5 is a coding and agent model released in standard and faster Lightning versions, with weights on Hugging Face under a modified MIT license. MiniMax reports 80.2% on SWE-Bench Verified and 76.3% on BrowseComp.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark on Cerebras hardware
items.summary: GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark is a smaller version of GPT-5.3-Codex built for real-time coding at over 1,000 tokens per second, and OpenAI's first model served on Cerebras rather than Nvidia hardware. It launched as a research preview for ChatGPT Pro users in Codex.
